newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Wife of self-exiled Nigerian editor reported held.
newsitem.headline: Wife of self-exiled Nigerian editor reported held.

text.p: The wife of a Nigerian opposition editor who fled the West African country in 1994 has been arrested, her sister said in a statement published on Saturday.
Four agents of the military intelligence arrested Ladi Olorunyomi on Thursday night and ransacked her Lagos home, said her sister Nana Suleiman.
"They did not give any reason for my sister's arrest," she said in the statement published in Nigerian newspapers.
There was no independent confirmation of the arrest. The security authorities normally refuse to comment on such issues.

Olorunyomi's husband Dapo Olorunyomi, an editor of the opposition magazine The News, fled to the United States fearing arrest over reports in the magazine about a coup plot to topple the military government.
Another editor of the magazine is serving a long jail term over the alleged coup plot along with more than 30 others, including retired General Olusegun Obasanjo, a former military ruler.
Nigeria's military government is under criticism at home and abroad over detentions without trial and the slow pace of its plan to return Africa's most populous nation to democracy.
